messages.subject: conducting a second level cfa
parts:
Hi there,

I do have an issue concerning a multilevel cfa.

I have just read that there is not yet a function for conducting a multilevel cfa in lavaan, but maybe one can deal with that issue and find another solution in lavaan.

I have a set of items which I related to 13 factors (facets) of the Big Five. The model fit is not the best but I guess I can deal with it (CFI: 0.775 (for a good model fit I should have 0.95), RMSEA (0.056 < 0.06) and SRMR (0.07 < 0.11).

The 13 facets should relate as well to some higher order latent factors of the Big Five.

I just conducted the first cfa. Is there a way that I can conduct a second level cfa?

Many thanks in advance!

Almut

messages.author: 12fbab588513996d
messages.subject: Re: conducting a second level cfa
parts:
Hi Almut,
If you would like to define the second-order variables, do it the same way as other first-order variables.

For example,
f1 =~ item1 + item2 + item3
f2 =~ item4 + item5 + item6 + item7
f3 =~ f1 + f2
In this example, the variables item1 to item7 are observed variables. Therefore, the latent variables f1 and f2 are ﬁrst-order factors. The latent variable f3 is a second-order factor,
since all of its indicators are latent variables themselves.
see:
http://users.ugent.be/~yrosseel/lavaan/lavaanJSSpreview.pdf
Page 6.
And don't forget specify the covariances if needed.
